subject: Energy
title: How a Nuclear Plant Generates Electricity
description: A short lesson to help you apply How a Nuclear Plant Generates Electricity.

hook.text: A nuclear plant is essentially a steam engine—fission heats water, steam spins a turbine, and drives a generator.

buildup.text: The reactor core heats water to about 320°C under high pressure—preventing it from boiling inside the reactor.

discovery.text: This hot water transfers heat to a secondary loop that produces steam—keeping radioactive water contained.

twist.text: The thermal efficiency is about 33%—similar to coal plants, because both are limited by thermodynamic constraints.

climax.text: A single large reactor produces about 1 gigawatt—enough to power a million homes continuously.

punchline.text: Split atoms, boil water, spin turbine—nuclear power is steam power.

quiz.question: How much power does a large nuclear reactor typically produce?
